title: High-Register Concessive Clauses: Jóllehet, Noha, and Ámbár

sections.title: The Structural Mechanism
sections.content: In C1 formal Hungarian essays and debates, plain *bár* or *de* often lacks the precision needed to weigh conflicting evidence. High-register concessive conjunctions like *jóllehet*, *noha*, and *ámbár* introduce a subordinate clause acknowledging a valid counter-point before the main thesis is affirmed: *Jóllehet a gazdasági mutatók javulnak, a társadalmi feszültségek nem enyhülnek.*

sections.title: Rhetorical Application & Stance
sections.content: Pay special attention to *holott*: unlike neutral *noha*, *holott* carries an adversative, almost indignant overtone, highlighting a stark contradiction between reality and expectation: *Mindenki elvárta a segítséget, holott senki sem tett érte semmit.*

sections.title: Patterns in Context
rows: Although the theory is appealing... (measured concession)
Even though he arrived late... (formal concession)
Albeit I acknowledge his merits... (elevated concession)
He didn't help, whereas he easily could have. (sharp contrast)
